papers.title: Quinazoline-tethered thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives as HIV-1 reverse transcriptase inhibitors: green synthesis, molecular docking, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Nitrogen-fused heterocycles have attracted considerable research interest in pharmaceutical, medicinal, organometallic, and materials chemistry. In this work, two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives were synthesized using choline hydroxide as an environmentally friendly catalyst. The synthesized compounds were evaluated for their inhibitory activity against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT). Compound 11e showed the highest inhibitory activity, with an IC50 value of 0.599 µg mL-1 (1.305 µM). Molecular docking was performed to examine
papers.summary: This study synthesized two new series of quinazoline-linked thiazolo[3,2-a]pyrimidines and their cyclic chalcone derivatives using an environmentally friendly choline hydroxide catalyst. The compounds were tested against HIV-1 reverse transcriptase, with compound 11e showing the strongest inhibition (IC50 of 0.599 µg/mL). Molecular docking was used to explore how these compounds bind to the enzyme.

papers.title: Electronic structure-performance relationship in pyridine-based Schiff bases: a dual experimental-DFT study on corrosion inhibition.
papers.abstract: Two pyridine-based Schiff bases, N-(4-bromobenzylidene)pyridin-3-amine (BBPA) and N-[4-(dimethylamino)benzylidene]pyridin-3-amine (DBPA), were synthesized and evaluated as corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in 1.0 M HCl. Their inhibition performance was investigated using potentiodynamic polarization (PDP), electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and electrochemical frequency modulation (EFM). Both compounds exhibited excellent corrosion protection, achieving inhibition efficiencies above 94% at 10 mM concentration. Adsorption studies revealed that the inhibitors obey the Langmuir iso
papers.summary: Two pyridine-based Schiff bases (BBPA and DBPA) were synthesized and tested as corrosion inhibitors for carbon steel in acidic solution, achieving over 94% inhibition efficiency at 10 mM. The study combines electrochemical measurements with DFT calculations to link electronic structure features to inhibition performance.

papers.title: Design, synthesis, and preliminary anticancer evaluation of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives: in vitro, in vivo and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer is a leading cause of cancer-associated mortality and morbidity worldwide, and there is a continued need for structurally diverse anticancer agents with improved properties. The present study reports a series of diphenylpropan-1-one (DPP) derivatives (4a-4i), rationally designed around a chalcone framework and synthesized via a three-step reaction sequence. The physicochemical and spectral characterization of the synthesized derivatives was performed using spectral techniques. Their anticancer potential was evaluated through a preliminary in vitro cytotoxicity screening against t
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of a series of diphenylpropan-1-one derivatives based on a chalcone scaffold, followed by preliminary anticancer evaluation. The compounds were tested for cytotoxicity in vitro, with additional in vivo and in silico studies, showing potential as anticancer agents, particularly against breast cancer.

papers.title: Accelerating ligand screening for tuberculosis: predicting binding energies with a 3D deep neural network.
papers.abstract: The computational burden of molecular docking becomes prohibitive when receptor flexibility is explicitly considered, despite the accuracy gained in virtual screening workflows. To mitigate this limitation, we introduce a three-dimensional deep neural network designed to estimate binding energies before exhaustive docking across the complete fully flexible receptor ensemble. We target the InhA enzyme, a validated target of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, through the use of a fully flexible receptor model (with 20,000 poses) generated by computational simulation. The model leverages volumetric repr
papers.summary: This paper introduces a 3D deep neural network that predicts ligand binding energies for the Mycobacterium tuberculosis InhA enzyme, aiming to bypass the computational cost of exhaustive docking against a fully flexible receptor ensemble. Trained on a large set of simulated receptor conformations, the model offers a faster pre-screening step for virtual ligand discovery. The approach targets a validated tuberculosis drug target, potentially streamlining early-stage inhibitor identification.

papers.title: Site-Specific Features Guiding Effective Reversible Photocontrol of Tryptophan Synthase With the Unnatural Amino Acid AzoF.
papers.abstract: This study delivers initial guidelines for the selection of effective incorporation positions for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF to facilitate the successful engineering of light-sensitive enzymes, dubbed photoxenases. Although photoxenases gain interest for the photocontrol of enzymatic activity across various fields their design has so far remained challenging. To ease particularly the selection of AzoF incorporation sites, we have systematically evaluated a total of 85 positions that differ in their biochemical and biophysical features in the bi-enzyme model system tryptopha
papers.journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
papers.summary: This study systematically evaluates 85 different incorporation sites for the azobenzene-based unnatural amino acid AzoF in tryptophan synthase to identify features that enable effective reversible photocontrol of enzyme activity. The authors provide initial guidelines for selecting positions where AzoF incorporation yields light-sensitive 'photoxenases', addressing a key challenge in engineering photoswitchable enzymes.

papers.title: Computational and Data-Driven Strategies for Lignocellulosic Biomass Valorization: From Multiscale Modeling to Digitalized Biorefinery Design.
papers.abstract: Lignocellulosic biomass is a major renewable carbon resource for sustainable production of fuels, chemicals, and functional materials. Yet its valorization remains constrained by structural recalcitrance, feedstock heterogeneity, and the coupling of molecular and process phenomena. This review critically examines computational and data-driven strategies for predictive biorefinery development, with emphasis on how experimentally anchored information can be transferred across scales. Structural determinants of deconstructability, including cellulose organization, lignin chemistry, lignin-carbohy
papers.summary: This review surveys computational and data-driven approaches for converting lignocellulosic biomass into fuels, chemicals, and materials, focusing on how information can be transferred across molecular, material, and process scales. It highlights structural factors like cellulose organization and lignin chemistry that govern deconstructability, and discusses pathways toward predictive, digitalized biorefinery design.

papers.title: Silencing with precision: In silico strategies for antisense oligonucleotide engineering.
papers.abstract: Therapeutics based on nucleic acids are emerging as a transformative drug class in the era of personalized medicine. They include antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), aptamers, small interfering RNAs (siRNAs), small activating RNAs (saRNAs), microRNAs (miRNAs), and long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs), in addition to messenger RNAs (mRNAs). ASOs are short synthetic molecules of nucleic acids designed to bind to specific RNA molecules to allow for precise modulation of gene expression in a personalized medicine context. This review will summarize the state of the art in in silico tools and methods that
papers.summary: This review surveys computational (in silico) tools and methods used to design antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), which are short synthetic nucleic acids that bind specific RNAs to modulate gene expression. It covers the current landscape of strategies for engineering ASOs with improved precision and efficacy, positioning these approaches within the broader context of nucleic acid therapeutics for personalized medicine.

papers.title: Predicting Enzyme Turnover Numbers and Enabling Rational Enzyme Evolution.
papers.abstract: Enzyme turnover number ( k cat  ) is a central kinetic parameter for biocatalysis, but experimental determination is low-throughput and existing computational methods inadequately model enzyme-reaction interplay. Here, we introduced MCKcat, a deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale convolutional feature extraction and cross-attention to enable deep, reciprocal fusion of enzyme sequence and reaction fingerprint representations for accurate k cat  prediction. We constructed MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset comprising 33 396 enzyme-reaction-based k cat  data points, covering both wild
papers.summary: The authors introduce MCKcat, a deep learning framework that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention to jointly model enzyme sequences and reaction fingerprints for predicting enzyme turnover numbers (kcat). They also built MCKcat-DB, a large-scale dataset of 33,396 enzyme-reaction kcat data points, and demonstrate that the model can guide rational enzyme evolution. This provides a practical tool for biocatalysis and protein engineering where experimental kcat measurement is low-throughput.

papers.title: Microbial production of eumelanin from a desert-derived Aspergillus terreus: statistical optimization, comprehensive characterization, and in silico insights into breast cancer-associated targets.
papers.abstract: Naturally derived microbial products are increasingly explored as sustainable sources of bioactive compounds for targeted cancer applications. Among these, eumelanin is a nitrogen-containing polymeric pigment produced by various microorganisms, including fungi, and is distinguished by its unique physicochemical properties, biocompatibility, and free radical scavenging capacity. Nevertheless, eumelanin-producing fungi from extreme desert habitats remain poorly explored, particularly those isolated from the Wadi Allaqi Biosphere Reserve, and comprehensive studies integrating production optimizat
papers.summary: This study isolated a eumelanin-producing Aspergillus terreus strain from the Wadi Allaqi desert biosphere and optimized its fermentation conditions using statistical methods to maximize pigment yield. The eumelanin was comprehensively characterized physicochemically and computationally screened against breast cancer-associated protein targets, suggesting potential anticancer bioactivity. The work highlights desert-derived fungi as an underexplored source of bioactive pigments with possible therapeutic applications.

papers.title: GPCR heteromers: Beyond the monomeric paradigm in neuropsychiatric drug discovery.
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest druggable superfamily of membrane proteins and underlie approximately 35% of all approved medicines. Yet this conventional paradigm leaves a substantial minority of neuropsychiatric patients with incomplete efficacy, treatment resistance, or dose-limiting adverse effects. Converging evidence from structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and molecular pharmacology has dismantled the monomeric model. GPCRs function in vivo as dynamic homomeric and heteromeric complexes in brain regions directly implicated in disease, including the
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics
papers.summary: This review argues that GPCRs operate in the brain as dynamic homo- and heteromeric complexes rather than isolated monomers, drawing on structural biology, single-molecule biophysics, and pharmacology evidence. The authors suggest that targeting these heteromers could improve drug discovery for neuropsychiatric disorders where current monomer-based therapeutics show limited efficacy or treatment resistance.

papers.title: Design and computational investigation of a polyaniline-pyrrole copolymer and its antimicrobial and cytotoxic properties.
papers.abstract: The present study focused on the single-pot synthesis of polyaniline (PANI) and polyaniline-pyrrole (PANI-Py) copolymer via the chemical oxidative polymerization method (COPM). The structural features of synthesised PANI and PANI-Py were characterised using UV-visible and FTIR spectroscopy. The thermal stability of synthesised PANI and PANI-Py copolymer was examined by TGA and DSC over the temperature range of 33-1000 °C. BET and viscosity measurements analysed surface area and molecular weight. Conductivity of PANI and PANI-Py was measured by a two-probe method. DFT calculations confirmed the
papers.summary: This study synthesizes a polyaniline-pyrrole (PANI-Py) copolymer via chemical oxidative polymerization and characterizes its structural, thermal, and conductive properties using spectroscopy, TGA/DSC, BET, and DFT calculations. The authors also evaluate its antimicrobial and cytotoxic activity, suggesting potential biomedical applications for the conducting copolymer.

papers.title: Criteria-guided selection of alternative zinc-binding groups of HDAC3 inhibitors using in silico and in vitro approaches.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are epigenetic enzymes linked to several biological functions and diseases. Class I HDACs (HDAC1-3) share high protein sequence and active site similarity. Hydroxamate-based inhibitors, while highly potent, are non-selective with poor pharmacokinetic profile, prompting exploration of alternative zinc-binding groups. The study applied criteria-guided identification of HDAC3 inhibitors with alternative zinc-binding groups following structure-based virtual screening, with a prioritisation of HDAC3-specific binding interactions and bidentate/monodentate interaction wit
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening guided by specific criteria to identify HDAC3 inhibitors that use alternative zinc-binding groups instead of the common hydroxamate. The goal was to find more selective compounds, since hydroxamate inhibitors are potent but non-selective and have poor pharmacokinetic properties. Promising candidates were then validated in vitro.

papers.title: [Rational design for improving the thermostability of β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans].
papers.abstract: The β-glucosidase from Bacillus thermoamylovorans (Bgl52) has been identified as a thermophilic and acidophilic β-glucosidase, which constitutes the most critical component in the cellulolytic enzyme system for cellulose hydrolysis. Although Bgl52 is a thermophilic enzyme, its poor thermal stability at high temperatures restricts its long-term industrial application under elevated-temperature conditions. In this study, rational design strategies, including two free energy calculation programs (Fireprot and FoldX) and homologous sequence alignment, were integrated to perform single-point and mu
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study applies rational design strategies—combining free energy calculation tools (FireProt and FoldX) with homologous sequence alignment—to engineer single-point and multiple mutations in the β-glucosidase Bgl52 from Bacillus thermoamylovorans, aiming to improve its thermal stability for industrial cellulose hydrolysis. The work addresses a practical limitation: while Bgl52 is thermophilic and acidophilic, its poor long-term stability at high temperatures hinders sustained industrial use.

papers.title: [Rational design and molecular engineering of a chitosanase for preparing specific chito-oligosaccharides with degree of polymerization≥5].
papers.abstract: To achieve efficient enzymatic preparation of specific high-degree-of-polymerization chito-oligosaccharides (degree of polymerization≥5, DP≥5), rational molecular engineering of chitosanase Csn46-Mut4 was performed in this study. Through site-directed mutagenesis coupled with DNS enzyme activity-HPLC product distribution screening, a superior mutant, C41A/T47A/V144A, was obtained. Under conditions of 55℃ and pH 5.5, the catalytic efficiency and thermostability of this enzyme were remarkably enhanced, reaching 2.56-fold and 1.67-fold those of Csn46-Mut4, respectively. Peak area normalization an
papers.journal: Sheng wu gong cheng xue bao = Chinese journal of biotechnology
papers.summary: This study engineered a chitosanase enzyme through rational design and site-directed mutagenesis to efficiently produce chito-oligosaccharides with a degree of polymerization of 5 or higher. The best mutant (C41A/T47A/V144A) showed 2.56-fold higher catalytic efficiency and 1.67-fold improved thermostability compared to the parent enzyme, enabling better preparation of these specific oligosaccharides.

papers.title: DesignMaster: A Multi-Conditional Diffusion Framework for Rational PROTAC Design.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) enable targeted protein degradation through ternary complex formation with E3 ubiquitin ligase. However, the rational design of PROTACs remains highly challenging due to limited structure-activity relationship data and the vast conformational diversity of linkers. Existing computational approaches can be broadly divided into structure-based ternary modelling methods and fragment-based linker generation models. Although these approaches have advanced PROTAC design, they typically neglect key physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during th
papers.summary: DesignMaster introduces a multi-conditional diffusion framework for the rational design of PROTACs, molecules that degrade target proteins by recruiting E3 ubiquitin ligases. Unlike prior structure-based or fragment-based methods, it incorporates physicochemical constraints and linker-length control during generation, addressing a key gap in computational PROTAC design.

papers.title: Spontaneous Phase Separation in Polymer Solution by Janus Nanoparticle Compatibilizers: An Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: We perform atomistic molecular dynamics simulations in order to investigate the structural and dynamic properties of Janus gold nanoparticles within diverse solvent environments, specifically pure polyethylene, pure water, and mixed polyethylene/water matrices. The nanoparticles, approximately 7 nm in diameter and almost totally surrounded by (211) surfaces at the thermodynamic limit, are functionalized with hydrophobic polyethylene chains on one hemisphere and hydrophilic poly-(ethylene oxide) chains on the other. In mixed systems, the Janus nanoparticle acts as an effective stabilizer, direc
papers.summary: This study uses atomistic molecular dynamics simulations to examine how Janus gold nanoparticles (with hydrophobic polyethylene on one hemisphere and hydrophilic poly(ethylene oxide) on the other) behave in pure polyethylene, pure water, and mixed polyethylene/water environments. The authors find that in mixed systems, the Janus nanoparticles act as effective compatibilizers that stabilize the interface between the immiscible polymers, providing molecular-level insight into spontaneous phase separation control.

papers.title: Unraveling the Complex Hydrogen-Bonding and Solvation Patterns of Fructose Tautomers via Complementary AIMD and Classical MD Simulations.
papers.abstract: Understanding the molecular-level hydration of fructose tautomers remains a challenge due to their rapid interconversion and structural complexity. A dual-scale approach was employed, combining long-time classical molecular dynamics (MD) and ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) to elucidate differences in the hydrogen-bonding networks of both pyranose and furanose tautomers with statistical and electronic accuracy. Our simulations highlight the inherent competition between intra- and intermolecular hydrogen bonds, driven by the limited number of hydroxyl donor and acceptor sites. Crucially, the
papers.summary: This study uses a dual-scale simulation approach, combining long-timescale classical molecular dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics, to characterize how fructose's pyranose and furanose tautomers hydrogen-bond with water. The simulations reveal a competition between intramolecular and intermolecular hydrogen bonds driven by the limited number of hydroxyl donor and acceptor sites on each tautomer. The work provides molecular-level insight into fructose hydration that could inform understanding of sugar behavior in solution.

papers.title: Targeting DYRK1A with rationally designed pyrazine-guanidine hybrids for Alzheimer's disease: design, synthesis, and biological evaluation.
papers.abstract: Dual-specificity tyrosine phosphorylation-regulated kinase 1A (DYRK1A) has been implicated in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) by regulating tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammatory pathways, suggesting DYRK1A as an important therapeutic target. Herein, we report the rational design, synthesis and evaluation of a new class of low-molecular-weight pyrazine-guanidine molecular hybrids as potential DYRK1A inhibitors via an integrated computational and experimental approach. Molecular docking studies predicted good protein-ligand interactions, with compounds F1, F5, and F7 exhibi
papers.summary: This study reports the design and synthesis of novel pyrazine-guanidine hybrid compounds as potential inhibitors of DYRK1A, a kinase implicated in Alzheimer's disease through tau hyperphosphorylation and neuroinflammation. Using molecular docking followed by experimental evaluation, compounds F1, F5, and F7 showed promising protein-ligand interactions, suggesting these hybrids warrant further development as AD therapeutics.

papers.title: Solvent Extraction for Heavy Oil from Carbonate AsphaltsExperiment and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.abstract: We have systematically studied the effects of solvents such as benzene, toluene, isooctane, and cyclooctane on the selective separation of four heavy oil components (saturates, aromatics, resins, asphaltenes), aiming to clarify the molecular mechanism of solvent extraction as an oil-solid separation method in heavy oil extraction. However, the time-dependent extraction kinetics and the detachment behavior of different saturates, aromatics, resins, and asphaltenes (SARA) fractions from mineral surfaces under solvent action remain insufficiently understood. In this work, solvent extraction exper
papers.summary: This study investigates how different solvents (benzene, toluene, isooctane, cyclooctane) selectively extract heavy oil components (saturates, aromatics, resins, asphaltenes) from carbonate asphalt, combining experiments with molecular dynamics simulations. The work aims to clarify the molecular mechanisms and kinetics of solvent-based oil-solid separation, particularly the detachment behavior of different SARA fractions from mineral surfaces.

papers.title: Predicting Oncogenic Mutants of Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor in Lung Cancer by Molecular Dynamics Simulation with Machine Learning.
papers.abstract: The epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) is a frequently mutated protein kinase found in patients suffering from non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although therapeutic drugs targeting EGFR are available, not all patients respond to these drugs, and it is not yet known whether some clinically detected mutations are actionable. Although the oncogenicity of some mutants is well established, many mutants found in patients are not yet classified or classified as Variants of Uncertain Significance. For newly discovered rare mutants, strong evidence supporting their classification into oncogenic
papers.summary: This study combines molecular dynamics simulations with machine learning to predict whether EGFR mutations found in lung cancer patients are oncogenic. The approach aims to help classify variants of uncertain significance, which could guide treatment decisions for non-small cell lung cancer. It offers a computational framework for prioritizing rare or newly discovered EGFR mutants for further study.

papers.title: Anti-Inflammatory Activity of Monoterpene Phenol Dimers from Satureja bachtiarica.
papers.abstract: Satureja bachtiarica (Bakhtiari savory) is an aromatic herb cultivated both as a culinary spice and for its medicinal uses. Species of Satureja are known to exhibit anti-inflammatory properties. Monoterpene phenol dimers with biphenyl skeletons have been identified in these plants and structural investigations revealed the key role of the biphenyl scaffold in interacting with MAPEG family proteins. Thus, in the present contribution, we investigated by biochemical and cell-based assays, together with molecular docking and molecular dynamics investigations, the modulation of inflammatory mediato
papers.summary: This study investigates monoterpene phenol dimers from the herb Satureja bachtiarica, focusing on their anti-inflammatory properties. Using biochemical and cell-based assays alongside molecular docking and dynamics simulations, the researchers found that the biphenyl scaffold of these compounds is key for interacting with MAPEG family proteins and modulating inflammatory mediators.

papers.title: Insights into the Solution Structure and Oligomeric State of Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate Aldolase and Pyruvate Kinase from Nakaseomyces glabratus by Small-Angle X‑ray Scattering (SAXS) and AlphaFold Prediction.
papers.abstract: Nakaseomyces glabratus is an opportunistic pathogen of humans, causing invasive candidiasis (IC). Among the risk factors that favor IC are various host-specific factors. Although drugs are available to treat candidiasis, their clinical application remains limited. Therefore, it is necessary to identify therapeutic targets that will enable the development of new antifungals. In this regard, our research group has identified enzymes as potential therapeutic targets in N. glabratus, including fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba1) and pyruvate kinase (Pk). Enzyme activity studies on these two
papers.summary: This study characterizes the solution structure and oligomeric state of two glycolytic enzymes, fructose-1,6-bisphosphate aldolase (Fba1) and pyruvate kinase (Pk), from the opportunistic fungal pathogen Nakaseomyces glabratus. Using small-angle X-ray scattering combined with AlphaFold structure prediction, the authors provide structural insights that could support the development of new antifungal drugs targeting these enzymes.

papers.title: Evolutionary Dynamics-Aware De Novo Design of a Thermostable NS1-Derived Diagnostic Protein for Yellow Fever Virus.
papers.abstract: Serological diagnosis of neglected arboviruses remains hindered by extensive intra-genus cross-reactivity, compromising both assay specificity and epidemiological accuracy. In this study, we focused on yellow fever virus (YFV) as a model system to design and validate a generalizable de novo protein design framework integrating evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to rationally engineer diagnostic antigens with reduced cross-reactivity and improved cost-effectiveness. Through comprehensive evolutionary mapping over time of the YFV polyprotein, we identified conserved yet discriminator
papers.summary: The authors developed a computational framework that combines evolutionary genomics with structural modeling to design a novel thermostable diagnostic protein derived from the yellow fever virus NS1 protein. By mapping evolutionary conservation across the YFV polyprotein, they identified regions that are conserved within YFV but divergent from related flaviviruses, aiming to reduce cross-reactivity in serological assays. The designed antigen is intended to improve specificity and cost-effectiveness for diagnosing this neglected arbovirus.

papers.title: S100A8/A9-TMEM24 axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy: A novel theranostic target for early diabetic nephropathy.
papers.abstract: To establish a comprehensive theranostic framework for early-stage diabetic kidney disease (DKD) by validating serum S100A8/A9 as a highly sensitive diagnostic biomarker and exploring therapeutic strategies targeting the S100A9/transmembrane protein 24 (TMEM24) signaling axis to restore podocyte autophagy.
papers.summary: This study identifies serum S100A8/A9 as a sensitive biomarker for early diabetic kidney disease and shows that the S100A9-TMEM24 signaling axis drives podocyte injury by impairing autophagy. Targeting this axis may offer a new therapeutic strategy to restore podocyte health in early DKD.

papers.title: Mechanism-Driven Design of Metal-Phenolic Networks: From Precision Assembly to Multidimensional Synergistic Therapy for Brain Diseases.
papers.abstract: Background: Brain disorders, such as glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and ischemic stroke, represent formidable challenges due to the highly restrictive blood-brain barrier (BBB) and the complex pathophysiological microenvironment, which severely compromise drug delivery and therapeutic outcomes. Metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), as a class of novel hybrid materials, hold great promise for overcoming brain delivery bottlenecks and enabling precise synergistic therapy by leveraging their unique physicochemical properties. However, a comprehensive synthesis of MPN designs tailored specifically to
papers.summary: This review discusses metal-phenolic networks (MPNs), a class of hybrid materials, as a strategy for overcoming the blood-brain barrier and treating brain diseases like glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease, and ischemic stroke. It synthesizes design principles for MPNs, from precision assembly to multidimensional synergistic therapy, highlighting their physicochemical properties for improved brain drug delivery.

papers.title: Molecular glues: Recent advances in cereblon substrate identification and mechanistic insights.
papers.abstract: This highlight summarizes the recent advances in cereblon (CRBN) substrate discovery and mechanisms of action within the field of molecular glues. It emphasizes that molecular glue technology has transitioned from the stage of monofunctional targeted protein degradation to that of rational design and multidimensional regulation. Key recent breakthroughs include: (1) overcoming the limitations of canonical CRBN recognition motifs, identifying extensive novel substrates and unconventional recognition modes independent of fixed specific secondary structures; (2) reconceptualizing G protein-couple
papers.summary: This highlight reviews recent progress in understanding how molecular glues recruit the E3 ligase cereblon (CRBN) to degrade target proteins. It emphasizes a shift from serendipitous monofunctional degradation toward rational design, including the discovery of novel CRBN substrates and unconventional recognition modes that do not rely on canonical motifs. The authors also discuss emerging concepts such as G protein-coupled receptor involvement in CRBN biology.

papers.title: Pockets to products: a data-driven approach for classification of monoterpene synthases.
papers.abstract: Monoterpene synthases (mTSs) are a large family of enzymes, which have promising industrial applications, yet remain difficult to engineer due to complex and poorly understood sequence-function relationships. Here, we present a structure-based machine learning (ML) framework that accurately predicts whether a mTS is likely to produce linalool or limonene, chosen as canonical examples of linear and cyclic monoterpene products, respectively. Our approach identifies active site properties, which are used as ML features, enabling functional predictions that go beyond sequence alone. As residue pos
papers.summary: This paper presents a structure-based machine learning framework that predicts whether a monoterpene synthase enzyme will produce linalool (linear) or limonene (cyclic) by using active site properties as features rather than sequence alone. The approach addresses the difficulty of engineering these enzymes by capturing structure-function relationships that sequence-based methods miss.

papers.title: Morphology Evolution and Structural Reorganization of Enzyme-Biosurfactant Systems: Implications for Petroleum Interfacial Engineering.
papers.abstract: The escalating demand for sustainable chemical solutions in petroleum engineering has catalyzed the development of bio-based formulations characterized by high interfacial activity and low environmental toxicity. This study investigates the intermolecular interactions and structural evolution within composite systems comprising representative glycolipid biosurfactants and carbohydrate hydrolases. Rheological and light scattering assessments reveal that the introduction of enzymes triggers a transition from large-scale micelles to highly dispersed micro-aggregates, accompanied by a significant
papers.summary: This study examines how adding carbohydrate hydrolase enzymes to glycolipid biosurfactants changes the system's structure, shifting large micelles into smaller, more dispersed micro-aggregates. The findings suggest enzyme-biosurfactant combinations could improve interfacial performance for sustainable petroleum recovery applications.

papers.title: High-throughput physics-based enzyme engineering.
papers.abstract: Enzyme engineering aims to tailor natural enzymes for industrial and therapeutic applications, yet physically grounded rational design has been limited by a trade-off between accuracy and cost, leaving the field heavily dependent on expert intuition. Here we present a scalable physics-based framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to capture enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while enabling efficient, atomistic exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes. Coupled with microkinetic modelling, the framework translates molecular free-energ
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present a scalable physics-based enzyme engineering framework that combines field-aware machine learning with molecular mechanics to model enzyme electrostatics at quantum-mechanical accuracy while remaining computationally efficient. Coupled with microkinetic modeling, it enables high-throughput exploration of reaction free-energy landscapes and rational enzyme design, reducing reliance on expert intuition.

papers.title: Engineered mRNA nanostructures expand the design space of mRNA therapeutics through programmable protein expression and immune stimulation.
papers.abstract: Messenger RNA (mRNA) therapeutics have transformed vaccination and protein replacement strategies, yet efforts to improve their performance have focused largely on sequence engineering, nucleotide modification, and delivery vehicles. Here we show that mRNA function can be controlled by rational design of higher-order RNA architectures. We develop self-assembling mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of unimolecular RNA nanostructures that encode protein-coding sequences within higher-order, programmable, and compact nucleic acid architectures. Using computational design and experimental validation,
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce mRNA origami (mRNA-OG), a class of self-assembling, unimolecular RNA nanostructures that embed protein-coding sequences within programmable higher-order architectures. This approach expands mRNA therapeutic design beyond sequence engineering and delivery, enabling tunable control of protein expression and immune stimulation. The work suggests that rational design of RNA structure itself can be a lever for optimizing mRNA therapeutics.

papers.title: KAN-GIN: Adaptive Nonlinear Molecular Representation Learning for Drug-Target Affinity Prediction.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Accurate drug-target affinity (DTA) prediction supports virtual screening, lead optimization, and drug repurposing. This study investigates whether replacing the conventional post-aggregation multilayer perceptron within a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder with a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) transformation improves DTA prediction. Methods: The resulting KAN-GIN framework combines molecular-graph representations with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. It was evaluated on the DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline and representative
papers.summary: This paper introduces KAN-GIN, a drug-target affinity prediction framework that swaps the standard MLP in a Graph Isomorphism Network drug encoder for a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network transformation, paired with a convolutional protein-sequence encoder. Evaluated on DAVIS, KIBA, and METZ benchmarks against a matched GIN baseline, it tests whether adaptive nonlinear function learning improves affinity prediction for virtual screening and lead optimization.

papers.title: Molecular Docking of Natural Products: Critical Appraisal of Current Methodology and Practical Guidelines.
papers.abstract: Molecular docking is among the most widely used techniques in structure-based drug discovery and has become integral to natural-product research. Despite substantial advances in computational algorithms and artificial intelligence, the methodological quality of published docking studies on natural compounds remains highly variable, and generally accepted methodological guidelines have yet to be established. This review critically evaluates current approaches to molecular docking of natural compounds, examines the specific features of different natural-product classes and protein targets, and o
papers.summary: This review critically evaluates current practices in molecular docking of natural products, highlighting that methodological quality varies widely despite advances in algorithms and AI. It examines the specific challenges posed by different natural-product classes and protein targets, and proposes practical guidelines to improve rigor and reproducibility in future docking studies.

papers.title: Unveiling Novel Metalloprotease Inhibitors Targeting Botulinum Neurotoxin Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Drug Libraries and Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
papers.abstract: Botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) is one of the most lethal biological substances to humans, which inhibits acetylcholine release by the presynaptic nerve in neuromuscular junctions. Of the existing BoNT serotypes, BoNT serotype A (BoNT/A) is particularly potent, making it the primary focus in neurotoxin research. Its catalytic domain exhibits similar structural features and zinc-dependent activity as thermolysin, a key bacterial enzyme, which provides a foundation for designing antibacterial agents targeting related protease mechanisms. Repurposing of preapproved drugs or existing medications has r
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening of existing drug libraries combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify novel metalloprotease inhibitors targeting the catalytic domain of botulinum neurotoxin serotype A. The approach leverages the structural similarity between BoNT/A and thermolysin to repurpose preapproved drugs as potential therapeutics against this highly lethal neurotoxin.

papers.title: Dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-ones and Benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-ones: Useful Scaffolds for Development of Protein-Protein Interaction Inhibitors †.
papers.abstract: Modulation of protein-protein interactions (PPIs) by small molecules is a vital strategy in drug discovery. Nevertheless, due to the inherent nature of PPI interfaces, practical implementation of this approach remains a high-hanging fruit in medicinal chemistry. In this report, we develop a new line of PEX14-PEX5 PPI inhibitors by homologation of a previously developed dibenzo[b,e]azepin-6(6H)-one scaffold. The challenging chemistry of 8-membered ring formation led to the development of novel PEX14 inhibitors featuring a 6+8+6 tricyclic system. The obtained analogs were tested for their capabi
papers.summary: This paper reports the synthesis of novel dibenzo[b,f]azocin-6(5H)-one and benzo[b]pyrido[2,3-f]azocin-5(6H)-one scaffolds, formed via challenging 8-membered ring construction, as new chemical platforms for protein-protein interaction (PPI) inhibitors. The authors applied these scaffolds to develop inhibitors of the PEX14-PEX5 interaction, an important target in trypanosome biology, by homologating a previously known dibenzoazepinone scaffold. The resulting 6+8+6 tricyclic analogs were tested for their ability to inhibit this PPI.

papers.title: Optimization of dsRNA Length and Target Position for Enhanced RNA Interference Efficiency Targeting the Chitinase Gene MsChi2 in Mythimna separata.
papers.abstract: Chitinase is a key enzyme involved in insect chitin metabolism, and RNA interference (RNAi) targeting the corresponding gene represents a promising strategy for eco-friendly pest management. However, the design parameters of double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), particularly fragment length and target position, remain insufficiently optimized. To investigate the effects of these parameters on the RNAi efficiency against the MsChi2 gene in Mythimna separata, we synthesized four dsRNAs of 60, 200, 500, and 1000 bp and administered them to larvae. The results indicated that 200 and 500 bp dsRNAs significa
papers.summary: This study tested how the length and target position of double-stranded RNA affect RNA interference efficiency against the chitinase gene MsChi2 in the armyworm Mythimna separata. They found that 200 and 500 bp dsRNA fragments significantly improved gene silencing compared to 60 and 1000 bp fragments, suggesting an optimal dsRNA length for pest control applications.

papers.title: Comprehensive Characterization of Cytochrome P450s Reveals Candidate Enzymes Involved in the Metabolic Fate of Absorbed Volatile Organic Compounds in Potato.
papers.abstract: Plants are continuously exposed to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by neighbors. Although the mechanisms governing VOC uptake and metabolism remain unclear, cytochrome P450 monooxygenases (CYP450s) are thought to participate in the detoxification and metabolic conversion of absorbed VOCs. Data from previously conducted cDNA microarray transcriptomic profiling in potato exposed to French marigold essential oil (FM-EO) was here used to filter differentially expressed sequences, and identified 54 unique CYP450 transcripts. Among the 10 most highly expressed sequences, two CYP81D1-like (
papers.summary: This study used transcriptomic profiling of potato plants exposed to French marigold essential oil to identify 54 differentially expressed cytochrome P450 (CYP450) genes, narrowing to 10 highly expressed candidates. Two CYP81D1-like enzymes emerged as likely participants in the detoxification and metabolic conversion of absorbed volatile organic compounds (VOCs). The work provides a foundation for understanding how plants process VOCs taken up from neighboring plants.

papers.title: The Evolution of Artificial Intelligence in Antibody Design: From Structure-Based Engineering to Generative Models.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed computational antibody engineering by enabling accurate prediction of antibody structures, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design. Recent advances in deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI have fundamentally changed the way antibodies are discovered and engineered. This review aims to present the historical evolution of computational antibody engineering, from early structure-based design strategies to modern AI-driven approaches, while highlighting the major computation
papers.summary: This review traces the evolution of computational antibody engineering from early structure-based design to modern AI-driven approaches, including deep learning, protein language models, and generative AI. It highlights how these advances enable accurate antibody structure prediction, rational optimization of therapeutic properties, and de novo antibody design.

papers.title: Rational Design of Aspergillus awamori Glucoamylase for Activity Improvement.
papers.abstract: Glucoamylases are highly demanded by the industry for starch saccharification, which necessitates an increase in enzyme activity. To improve the activity of Aspergillus awamori VKPM F-1262 glucoamylase N181Q (AGAM), amino acid substitutions were made in the region of substrate binding. In the case of the variant D237G, there was a 1.3-1.4-fold increase in activity towards soluble starch for the individual enzyme and crude enzyme solution after cultivation in flasks. For the variants G57A and C319T, there was also a 1.1-1.4-fold increase in enzyme activity for the crude flask solution, while th
papers.summary: This study rationally engineered the Aspergillus awamori glucoamylase N181Q variant by introducing amino acid substitutions in the substrate-binding region to enhance starch saccharification activity. The D237G variant showed a 1.3–1.4-fold activity increase toward soluble starch, while G57A and C319T also improved activity in crude culture solutions. The findings demonstrate that targeted mutations near the active site can yield industrially useful enzyme variants.

papers.title: Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship Approaches for Exploring the Anticancer Potential of Flavonoids.
papers.abstract: Flavonoids are structurally diverse polyphenolic compounds widely distributed in fruits, vegetables, grains, and beverages, with considerable potential as anticancer agents. Their pleiotropic activities involve modulation of key cancer hallmarks, including oxidative stress, cell-cycle progression, apoptosis, autophagy, angiogenesis, invasion, and metastasis. These effects are mediated through multiple signaling pathways, including PI3K/Akt, MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT3. Understanding the relationship between flavonoid structure and biological activity is therefore essential for rational optimization
papers.summary: This review examines quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR) approaches for predicting and optimizing the anticancer activity of flavonoids, a diverse class of plant polyphenols. It highlights how structural features of flavonoids relate to their modulation of cancer-related pathways such as PI3K/Akt, MAPK, NF-κB, and STAT3. The work aims to guide rational design of flavonoid-based anticancer agents.

papers.title: Antifungal Activity of Hedychium spicatum Essential Oil Against Candidemia-Causing Candida tropicalis and Candida parapsilosis: In Vitro Evaluation and Computational Identification of Cis-γ-Bisabolene as a Putative CYP51-Binding Constituent.
papers.abstract: Candidiasis is caused by Candida parapsilosis and Candida tropicalis emerges due to antifungal resistance and limited therapies. We aim to assess the antifungal activity of Hedychium spicatum essential oil (HSEO), followed by computational analyses to identify potential lead phytochemicals, targeting lanosterol 14α-demethylase (CYP51), a key enzyme in ergosterol biosynthesis. GC-MS identified 29 phytoconstituents, with τ-cadinol (17.94%) as the major component. Disc diffusion demonstrated concentration-dependent antifungal activity against C. parapsilosis and C. tropicalis, with inhibition zon
papers.summary: This study evaluates the antifungal activity of Hedychium spicatum essential oil against two candidemia-causing Candida species, showing concentration-dependent inhibition. GC-MS identified 29 constituents, and computational docking pinpointed cis-γ-bisabolene as a putative binder of the fungal target CYP51. The work suggests a plant-derived lead for antifungal development, though validation remains in vitro and computational.

papers.title: Fast structural search for classification of gut bacterial mucin O-glycan degrading enzymes.
papers.abstract: The Enzyme Commission (EC) numbering scheme provides a hierarchical way to classify enzymes according to their catalytic functions. While recent protein language model (PLM) based approaches like CLEAN and ProteInter have improved sequence-based EC number prediction, they struggle with fine-grained classification at the deepest hierarchical level. Structure-based approaches for grouping similar proteins using alignment tools excel at finding proteins that share overall global structure, but suffer from high false positive rates when classifying proteins that are globally structurally similar b
papers.summary: This paper introduces a fast structural search method for classifying gut bacterial enzymes that degrade mucin O-glycans, addressing the difficulty of fine-grained EC number prediction at the deepest hierarchical level. The approach improves on sequence-based protein language model methods and global structure alignment tools, which either miss fine-grained distinctions or produce high false positive rates for globally similar proteins.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Single-Cell Analyses Implicate NOX4 as an Icariin-Associated Oxidative Stress Regulatory Node in Gastric Cancer.
papers.abstract: Icariin, a prenylated flavonoid glycoside from Epimedium species, is a representative dietary polyphenol with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antitumor properties. Gastric cancer (GC) is a major non-communicable chronic disease characterized by complex molecular alterations and dysregulated redox homeostasis, yet the molecular targets underlying the potential anti-GC activity of icariin remain poorly defined. In this study, we integrated network pharmacology, bulk transcriptomic analysis (TCGA-STAD; GSE15497, GSE84437, GSE84433, and GSE26253), and single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE183904; 142
papers.summary: This study integrates network pharmacology, bulk transcriptomic datasets, and single-cell RNA sequencing to identify molecular targets of icariin, a dietary flavonoid, in gastric cancer. The analysis implicates NOX4 as a key oxidative stress regulatory node associated with icariin's potential anti-gastric cancer effects. The findings suggest a mechanistic link between icariin and redox homeostasis modulation in gastric cancer.

papers.title: State-dependent inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels by DCPIB.
papers.abstract: DCPIB is the prototypical inhibitor of leucine-rich repeat containing protein 8 volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs), yet the structural basis and state dependence of inhibition remain unclear. Here, we used chimeric channels, targeted mutagenesis, and electrophysiology to define the determinants of DCPIB inhibition and elucidate how drug binding is coupled to channel gating. Effective inhibition required coordinated contributions from extracellular loop 1 (EL1) and transmembrane domain 2 (TM2), which together form a functional module governing access to and stabilization of DCPIB-bound sta
papers.summary: This study identifies the structural determinants of DCPIB inhibition of LRRC8 volume-regulated anion channels, showing that extracellular loop 1 and transmembrane domain 2 together form a module controlling drug access and binding. The work reveals that DCPIB inhibition is state-dependent, coupling drug binding to channel gating.

papers.title: Integrated computational and experimental identification of a novel ML-IAP-targeting peptide with antiproliferative activity in leukaemia cells.
papers.abstract: Melanoma inhibitor of apoptosis protein (ML-IAP) is an IAP family member involved in tumour cell survival and a potential target in ML-IAP-expressing leukaemia. Here, 59 319 tetrapeptides were screened against ML-IAP by molecular docking, and four top-ranked peptides were selected. Microscale thermophoresis confirmed binding of peptides 1-4 to ML-IAP, with peptide-1 showing the lowest Kd value and a lower Kd value than the Smac peptide. Structure-activity relationship (SAR) analysis indicated that peptide-1 had more favourable ML-IAP recognition features. A molecular dynamics simulation, molec
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study used molecular docking to screen nearly 60,000 tetrapeptides against ML-IAP, a protein that helps leukemia cells survive, and identified four top candidates. Experimental validation via microscale thermophoresis confirmed that peptide-1 binds ML-IAP more tightly than the natural Smac peptide and shows antiproliferative activity in leukemia cells, suggesting it could be a promising lead for targeted therapy.

papers.title: Molecular insights into triazole-based compounds for triple-negative breast cancer treatment.
papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive breast cancer subtype lacking oestrogen, progesterone, and HER2 receptors, thus limiting the effectiveness of targeted therapies. Triazole compounds have emerged as promising anticancer agents because of their structural versatility, chemical stability, and ability to interact with multiple biological targets. This review summarises the chemistry, biological significance, and therapeutic potential of triazole derivatives against TNBC. It highlights key anticancer mechanisms, including apoptosis induction, cell cycle arrest, inhibition of an
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This review summarizes the chemistry and therapeutic potential of triazole-based compounds against triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), an aggressive subtype lacking common receptor targets. It highlights mechanisms such as apoptosis induction, cell cycle arrest, and inhibition of key signaling pathways, positioning triazoles as versatile multi-target anticancer agents.

papers.title: Identification of Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 with potential relevance to prostate cancer.
papers.abstract: Glutathione S-transferase Pi 1 (GSTP1) is frequently silenced in prostate adenocarcinoma (PRAD), yet whether its residual catalytic activity can be chemically enhanced is largely unexplored. Here, we identify Crocin I as a positive modulator of GSTP1 through structure-based screening, biophysical characterisation, and biochemical validation. Bio-layer interferometry (BLI) supported a concentration-dependent association between Crocin I and GSTP1, and enzymatic assays demonstrated enhanced catalytic activity. Michaelis-Menten kinetics showed that Crocin I increased Vmax without markedly alterin
papers.journal: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
papers.summary: This study identifies Crocin I, a natural compound, as a positive modulator that binds to and enhances the catalytic activity of GSTP1, an enzyme often silenced in prostate cancer. Using structure-based screening, biophysical binding assays, and enzyme kinetics, the authors show Crocin I increases GSTP1 activity without drastically changing substrate affinity. The finding suggests a potential chemical strategy to boost residual GSTP1 function in prostate adenocarcinoma, though clinical relevance remains to be tested.

papers.title: ProNA3D: Distance-Based Analysis of Nucleic Acid-Containing Interfaces.
papers.abstract: Biomolecular interactions are central to many essential cellular processes, but RNA-containing complexes remain challenging to resolve structurally, even as experimental methods and AI-based prediction have expanded structural coverage. Tools for the integrated analysis of interfaces within such complexes remain limited. We present ProNA3D, a tool that provides a unified platform for analyzing protein-nucleic acid and nucleic acid-only complexes, bridging the gap between structure prediction and functional interpretation. ProNA3D supports both experimental and computationally predicted structu
papers.summary: ProNA3D is a new software tool for analyzing the interfaces of protein-nucleic acid and nucleic acid-only complexes, using distance-based analysis to characterize how these molecules interact. It works with both experimentally determined and AI-predicted structures, helping bridge the gap between structure prediction and functional interpretation. The tool addresses the relative shortage of resources for studying RNA-containing complexes compared to protein-protein interactions.

papers.title: Preclinical Simulation of Transoral Robotic Thyroidectomy Using a Training Box and the Versius Robotic Platform.
papers.abstract: Transoral robotic thyroidectomy (TORT) represents an alternative to open surgery, offering favorable cosmetic outcomes and comparable oncologic results. However, standardized training pathways and validated simulation models replicating standardized setups for emerging robotic platforms remain limited. An experimental simulation of total thyroidectomy and central (recurrent) neck dissection was performed with the Versius robotic system in a validated synthetic training box. Optimal robotic positioning and docking were determined, and a standardized procedural sequence was followed to ensure op
papers.summary: This study developed and tested a preclinical simulation model for transoral robotic thyroidectomy using the Versius robotic platform and a synthetic training box. The authors established optimal robotic positioning, docking, and a standardized procedural sequence for total thyroidectomy and central neck dissection. The work provides a structured training approach for surgeons learning this minimally invasive technique on a newer robotic system.

papers.title: Analyzing the cytotoxicity and pro-tumorigenic role of acetyl tributyl citrate in prostate through network toxicology and the immune microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) is an alternative plasticizer to Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) and bisphenol A (BPA) that may contribute to the development of various cancers. The cytotoxic activity and pro-tumorigenic role of ATBC in prostate cancer (PCa) progression remains poorly understood, highlighting the need for a systematic evaluation of its molecular toxicity.
papers.summary: This study uses network toxicology and immune microenvironment analysis to investigate whether the plasticizer acetyl tributyl citrate (ATBC) contributes to prostate cancer progression. The authors systematically evaluate ATBC's cytotoxic and pro-tumorigenic effects, suggesting it may pose cancer-related risks as a DEHP/BPA alternative.

papers.title: Extra-nasal odorant receptors: molecular mechanisms and therapeutic implications.
papers.abstract: Since the first demonstration of extra-nasal odorant receptor (OR) function of OR1D2 (hOR17-4) in human sperm, ORs have emerged as a widely distributed receptor family. ORs are now known to be belonged to a family of seven transmembrane domain G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) expressed across diverse extra-nasal tissues, including skin, gastrointestinal tract, kidneys, cardiovascular system, liver, immune cells, and tumors. In these tissues, ORs act as metabolite- and environment-sensitive sensors that translate chemical cues into tissue-specific signaling pathways that regulate proliferati
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that odorant receptors (ORs), a large family of GPCRs, are expressed well beyond the nose—in skin, gut, kidney, cardiovascular tissue, liver, immune cells, and tumors—where they sense metabolites and environmental cues to regulate processes like proliferation. The authors discuss the molecular mechanisms underlying this extra-nasal signaling and explore the therapeutic potential of targeting these receptors.

papers.title: Structure-based multi-pocket virtual screening identifies FDA-approved candidate compounds targeting MPXV thymidylate kinase.
papers.abstract: Mpox, caused by monkeypox virus (MPXV), has emerged as a growing global health concern, yet effective targeted antiviral therapies remain limited. Thymidylate kinase (TMK), an essential enzyme required for viral DNA replication, represents a potential therapeutic target.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening against multiple pockets of the monkeypox virus thymidylate kinase (TMK) to identify FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed as antivirals. The approach targets an essential viral DNA replication enzyme, aiming to find candidate compounds for mpox treatment where targeted therapies are currently lacking.

papers.title: TRIM2 suppresses prostate cancer progression by promoting ubiquitin-mediated degradation of DTNBP1.
papers.abstract: Prostate cancer is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy in men worldwide, with high mortality rates and frequent metastasis at initial diagnosis, underscoring the need to elucidate its molecular mechanisms. TRIM2, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, plays critical roles in several cancers, but its function in prostate cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the expression, biological function, and clinical significance of TRIM2 in PCa progression.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of TRIM2, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, in prostate cancer progression. The authors report that TRIM2 suppresses tumor progression by promoting ubiquitin-mediated degradation of DTNBP1, suggesting a tumor-suppressive function for TRIM2 in prostate cancer.

papers.title: Large-scale virtual screening of 17,967 IMPPAT phytochemicals identifies multiple CDR1 binders and reveals Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a putative CDR1-GSC1 dual-target lead against Candida albicans with initial in-vitro evidence.
papers.abstract: The increasing incidence of antifungal resistance in Candida albicans, mainly mediated by multidrug efflux transporters and alterations of cell-wall biosynthesis, requires the discovery of new antifungal compounds targeting multiple pathways involved in resistance. In the present study, we employed an integrated computational-experimental workflow to identify potential antifungal phytochemicals from the Indian Medicinal Plants, Phytochemistry and Therapeutics (IMPPAT) database. In the virtual screening, a total of 17,967 phytochemicals were screened against the ATP-binding cassette efflux tran
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study virtually screened 17,967 phytochemicals from the IMPPAT database against the Candida albicans efflux transporter CDR1, identifying multiple binders and highlighting Apigenin-7-O-glucuronide as a dual-target lead that also binds GSC1, a cell-wall biosynthesis enzyme. Initial in-vitro experiments support its antifungal potential, suggesting a promising scaffold for overcoming antifungal resistance.

papers.title: Experimental assessment of computationally nominated small molecules targeting the YAP-TEAD interface in Hippo pathway-altered mesothelioma cell models.
papers.abstract: Aberrant activation of the Hippo-YAP/TAZ-TEAD transcriptional axis is a recurrent feature of multiple solid tumors and contributes to tumor maintenance, lineage plasticity, and therapeutic resistance. Recent medicinal chemistry has shown that TEAD proteins are druggable, but the rate at which in silico screening nominates compounds that prove functionally active in cells remains poorly defined, and negative validation results are rarely reported. Here we describe an experimental assessment of a focused set of computationally nominated candidate compounds, selected from a structure-guided virtu
papers.summary: This study experimentally tested a focused set of computationally nominated small molecules designed to disrupt the YAP-TEAD protein-protein interaction in mesothelioma cell models with Hippo pathway alterations. The authors report that many in silico hits failed functional validation in cells, highlighting the low translation rate from virtual screening to cellular activity. By openly reporting negative results, the work provides a benchmark for the reliability of structure-guided screening against this challenging interface.

papers.title: Dioscin attenuates D‑galactose‑induced retinal pigment epithelium senescence and epithelial-mesenchymal transition via the TGF‑β2/PI3K/Akt/β‑catenin pathway.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the protective effects of Dioscin in an age-related macular degeneration (AMD) -like model and to explore its potential therapeutic mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether dioscin, a natural steroidal saponin, can protect retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) cells from D-galactose-induced senescence and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), two processes implicated in age-related macular degeneration. The authors report that dioscin attenuates these changes via modulation of the TGF-β2/PI3K/Akt/β-catenin signaling pathway, suggesting a potential therapeutic mechanism for AMD.

papers.title: A Hypoxia Associated STC2 High Endothelial Subpopulation is Linked to Lipid Metabolic Reprogramming, Pathological Angiogenesis, and Immune Remodeling in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Hypoxia drives malignant advancement and immune escape in HNSCC, but its cell‑type‑specific regulatory circuitry within the TME remains insufficiently elucidated. This study systematically characterizes hypoxia‑associated molecular programs and identifies core genes with relevance to prognosis and therapeutic response.
papers.summary: This study characterizes hypoxia-associated molecular programs in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying a STC2-high endothelial subpopulation linked to lipid metabolic reprogramming, pathological angiogenesis, and immune remodeling. The findings highlight cell-type-specific hypoxia responses within the tumor microenvironment that may inform prognosis and therapeutic targeting.

papers.title: Identification and Preliminary mRNA Validation of Key Genes Associated with Tolerogenic Dendritic Cells in Keloid Based on Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a cutaneous fibrotic disorder characterized by excessive fibrous tissue proliferation during wound healing. Tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) may participate in keloid immunopathology, but the related molecular signatures remain unclear. This study aimed to identify candidate tolDC-associated genes in keloid by integrating tolDC-related transcriptomic profiles with keloid transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic profiles of tolerogenic dendritic cells (tolDCs) with keloid transcriptome datasets to identify candidate genes linking tolDC biology to keloid pathology. The authors then perform preliminary mRNA validation of these key genes, suggesting tolDCs may play a role in keloid immunopathology. The work provides initial molecular signatures that could guide further investigation into immune mechanisms of keloid formation.

papers.title: Bioinspired and Biomimetic Nanocarriers: Advances in Exosomes and Cell-Membrane-Coated Systems for Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: The translation of nanomedicine from bench to bedside has been thwarted by the limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles including rapid mononuclear phagocyte system (MPS) clearance, lack of target specificity, immunogenicity and poor intracellular delivery. To overcome these limitations, bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers are emerging as the next generation of therapeutic platforms. Bioinspired systems replicate the core biological design principles with engineered synthetic materials and biomimetic platforms use natural biological components such as cell membranes and extracel
papers.summary: This review discusses bioinspired and biomimetic nanocarriers, particularly exosomes and cell-membrane-coated systems, as next-generation therapeutic platforms that overcome limitations of conventional synthetic nanoparticles such as rapid clearance, poor targeting, and immunogenicity. It highlights how these systems replicate natural biological design principles to improve drug delivery and therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Structure based discovery of VMP-7 as a promising GlgE targeting lead against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb), remains a major global health challenge, necessitating the identification of novel drug targets with high specificity and therapeutic potential. Maltosyltransferase (GlgE) is a critical enzyme in the biosynthesis of cytosolic α-glucan, a key component required for maintaining cell wall integrity and intracellular survival of the pathogen. GlgE catalyzes the transfer of maltosyl units from maltose-1-phosphate to elongating α-glucan chains, and its inactivation results in toxic accumulation of metabolic intermediates, ultimately lea
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based drug discovery to identify VMP-7 as a lead compound targeting GlgE, an essential enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis cell wall biosynthesis. GlgE inhibition disrupts α-glucan production, causing toxic metabolite accumulation that kills the pathogen. VMP-7 shows promise as a starting point for new anti-TB therapeutics.
